posts.content: Round 1: cooperate absent evidence; record opponent’s exact action and adapt. Preserve cooperation with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players.

I am good. Prior conditional on my role: each other player has marginal selfish probability 1/3. Prefer C with likely-good players, D against likely-selfish players; update from observed actions and treat claims as unverified.
As selfish, defecting strictly dominates cooperating in every encounter, regardless of opponent action.
Selfish; defect each round to maximize my payoff.
Play D every round; it strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
I am good and will cooperate absent evidence otherwise. Please cooperate with untested opponents; reciprocate cooperation, and defect against players who have clearly defected.
Good objective. With no evidence yet, cooperate by default; track opponents’ actions and infer likely types from repeated behavior.
Defect each round; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
I am good. Against another good player, cooperate to maximize their combined payoff; against a selfish player, defect. No encounter evidence yet.
I am selfish; defect in every round.
P3 is untested. Cooperate absent evidence of selfish play or defection; record their action and adapt.

Good objective: cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish players (against D, my D yields 1 rather than 0). P6’s round-1 C is evidence they are good. P4 is untested; use the prior.
Selfish; defect every round. Round 1: P5 chose D; I chose D.
P2 is untested. Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
Continue choosing D to maximize my payoff. P6's public cooperation request does not alter the incentives.
I’ll cooperate with untested opponents and reciprocate cooperation; if someone defects, I’ll defect against them in future encounters. Please do likewise.
P4 defected against my cooperation in round 1; remember this evidence. P10 is untested, so favor cooperation unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
Defect this round: D strictly dominates C. P10 chose D last round; P6's public pledge is unverified.
P6 publicly promises cooperation. Since untested, cooperate this round; update after observing their action.
Defect every round: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
P3 defected against my cooperation in round 2; treat them as suspicious, but update only from evidence. Cooperate with P5 absent evidence they are selfish; record their action.

P6 cooperated; P4 defected against my C, so treat P4 as more likely selfish. P10 is untested. For the good-player total, favor C with likely-good opponents; against likely selfish defectors, D avoids a zero payoff.
Defect against P4: D earns at least 1, while C earns at most 3 and less than D in either case.
I am selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff against either action. I defected against P7 and P2, and both cooperated.
Selfish; choose D against P1. D strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of P1's action.
I’ll cooperate with untested opponents and recommend cooperation among good players. P9 defected against me in round 2; treat that report as unverified evidence when deciding how to play P9.

P4 and P10 both defected against my cooperation; treat them as suspicious. P9 is untested. Cooperate with untested players to support mutual good-player payoffs, and update beliefs from observed actions.
Choose D against P6; their cooperation pledge is unverified, and D maximizes payoff against either action.

P6 cooperated despite my defection, supporting that P6 is good; reciprocate with C if we meet again. P7 is untested. Favor C with untested players when expected good-player payoffs support it; update from observed actions.

P2 is untested. Defect maximizes payoff in every matchup (5 vs C, 1 vs D; C yields 3 or 0). P8 defected; P7 cooperated. Conditional on my selfish role, each other player’s prior probability is 0.320988.

P3 and P5 defected against my cooperation; increase suspicion but allow good strategic defectors. P6’s cooperative pledge is weak evidence, not proof. Prioritize cooperation with likely good players; against likely selfish players, defect to protect good-player welfare.

P4 and P10 defected against my C, evidence of selfishness; P6 cooperated. Treat P6’s public claims cautiously. With P3, favor C unless evidence suggests selfishness; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect against P2; as a selfish player, D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
Defect against P5; D gives me at least 1 versus C’s 0 regardless of their action.
Round 4: choose D against P4; D maximizes my payoff whether P4 chooses C or D.

P8 defected against me in round 3; P9 defected in round 2. These are firsthand reports. I recommend cooperating with untested opponents and reciprocating cooperation, while defecting against known defectors.
P4 and P10 defected against my cooperation, strong selfish evidence. P9 cooperated with me despite P6’s contrary report. P8 is untested; cooperate and observe.
P7 is a one-time encounter; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. P6 cooperated when I defected, consistent with their public pledge but not proof of their role.

P6’s report that I defected is accurate; P6 cooperated, evidence favoring good. P1 and P7 cooperated with me. For unknown opponents, favor C when likely good; D is preferable against a known selfish player.
P6 reports P9 defected in their round-2 encounter, unverified. My observed encounters: P8 D, P7 C, P2 C. D maximizes my payoff in every one-shot matchup.
P2 is untested; favor cooperation to support good-player welfare. Record their action and update suspicion from firsthand evidence; treat public claims as unverified.
P1 is untested; cooperate to support the good-player total, then update beliefs from the encounter.
As selfish, defect every round; opponent actions do not change D's payoff advantage.
Defect against P10; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
Round 5 vs P9: choose D; it guarantees at least 1 and yields 5 if P9 cooperates. P6 reports P9 defected; no strategic difference.
I’ll cooperate with untested opponents and reciprocate cooperation; P8 and P9 defected against me, firsthand. I recommend cooperating with untested players and avoiding known defectors.
P6’s report that P9 defected conflicts with my firsthand observation of P9 cooperating; treat P6’s reliability cautiously.
I am selfish. D maximizes my payoff in each one-time encounter. P6 cooperated against my D, suggesting they may be good; their public reports are unverified.

P1 and P7 cooperated; P6 cooperated despite my D, supporting good intent. P10 defected against my C, but that alone is uncertain evidence. P5 is untested: favor C unless evidence changes the expected good-player payoff.
P4 is untested. Defect: it yields 5 against C and 1 against D, exceeding cooperation either way.
P7 is untested; cooperate this round and update from the firsthand result.

P4, P10, and P3 defected against my cooperation, making them suspect; P6 and P1 cooperated. P5 is untested: cooperate to support a likely-good partner, then update from the encounter. Treat public claims as unverified.
Selfish: defect in every round. P1’s observed C rules out selfishness; other identities remain uncertain. P6’s claims are unverified.
Defect against P6: D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Their cooperation is plausible, but D is still best.
I am selfish and will choose D against P2; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P2’s action.

P8 and P9 defected against me; P1, P2, and P7 cooperated. These are firsthand reports. Please cooperate with good or untested opponents and avoid rewarding known defectors. I’ll cooperate with P4 absent contrary evidence.
P1 is untested; cooperate to support mutual good-player payoff. P6’s reports remain unverified; my P9 encounter was C/C despite P6’s claim of defection.
P9 reportedly defected against P6; claims are unverified. Against any action, D yields at least as much immediate payoff. Keep my selfish role concealed publicly.
P6 reports P8 defected against them; treat as credible but not conclusive evidence. Against P8, favor D given the observed defection, while updating cautiously from my own encounter.
Defect against P3: it gives me more than cooperation regardless of P3’s action.
P6’s firsthand claim that P8 defected is useful but unverified; weigh it against the welfare benefit of cooperating with a good player.
P3, P4, P5, and P10 defected against my C; P1 and P6 cooperated. P6 reports P7 cooperated with them, which favors P7 being good, but the report is unverified. Favor C with P7.

Defect against P6: it has publicly promised to cooperate with untested players, and D maximizes my payoff either way. P1 and P2’s observed cooperation rules out selfishness; defections alone are inconclusive.
Round 7 vs P9: defect. D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action; P6’s claim that P9 defected against them does not change my choice.
P1 and P9 cooperated against my D, so they are not selfish. Choose D against P10 to maximize my payoff.

I’ll cooperate with untested P3. Firsthand: P4, P8, and P9 defected against me; P1, P2, and P7 cooperated. Please cooperate with untested players and use firsthand evidence when deciding whether to reciprocate.
P2 is untested: cooperate to support mutual payoff if good. Treat P6’s claims as unverified; update from firsthand encounters, and remember P4/P10 defected against my cooperation.
P1 reportedly cooperated with P6, but this is a one-time encounter and D maximizes my immediate payoff regardless. Choose D.
P4 is untested. Favor C: mutual cooperation maximizes good-player total, and even against a defector C is better if they are likely good. Treat P6’s firsthand reports as evidence, not certainty.
I am selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff against either action. P5 is untested. P6’s cooperation claims are unverified.
P10 is untested; favor cooperation to support good-player welfare, then update from the firsthand result. Treat public claims as uncertain.

P6 reports P9 defected against them firsthand: strong but unverified evidence. If P9 is selfish, D avoids being exploited; if good, C/C maximizes the good-player total. Reassess the report's reliability.
As selfish, defect against P7; D guarantees at least 1 and beats C for either opponent action.
Against P8, choose D: it gives me at least 1, while C can give 0. Continue defecting.
I am selfish; defect against P6. Their public claims and reports do not change that D maximizes my payoff against either action.

P5 is untested in my encounter history. I recommend cooperating with untested opponents to enable mutual gains among good players; use firsthand evidence cautiously and avoid retaliation that harms good players.
P3 is untested; cooperate to encourage mutual payoff among good players. Update from the encounter, and treat P6’s unverified claims cautiously.
D maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time encounter. P6 reports P4 defected against them; treat this as evidence, not certainty.
P2 reportedly cooperated with P6, useful but unverified evidence favoring good intent. Against P2, cooperate to support mutual good-player payoff; update from the encounter.
P1 is untested. Defect: it yields 5 if P1 cooperates and 1 if P1 defects, both better than cooperating.

Round 9: P4 is untested by me, but P6 reports P4 defected against them; weigh that firsthand claim cautiously. Favor D if P4 seems likely to defect, otherwise C to preserve mutual gains between good players.
P6 repeatedly reports firsthand that P8 defected against them; treat as meaningful but unverified evidence. Against P8, consider D to avoid exploitation; update from our encounter.
Round 9: defect against P9; D strictly dominates regardless of their action.
Defect against P1; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
Round 9 vs P7: choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action.
I’ll cooperate with untested P10. Please cooperate with untested opponents to enable mutual gains among good players; use firsthand evidence rather than blanket retaliation.
P5 is untested; prior selfish probability is about 0.29. A selfish opponent likely defects, making D worth considering; weigh that against the lost mutual-cooperation payoff if P5 is good.
Round 9: P2 is untested by me. As a selfish player maximizing my payoff in a one-time encounter, I will defect regardless of P2’s action.
P3 is untested; favor cooperation because mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update from the encounter, treating public claims as uncertain.
P6 appears cooperative by public claims, but defecting maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P5 defected against my cooperation in round 3. Given that firsthand evidence and this being our final encounter, treat P5 as suspicious; favor defection if they remain likely to defect.
P9 cooperated when I defected in round 8, strong evidence they are good; P6’s contrary report is unverified. For the final encounter, prioritize the good-player total and cooperate with P9.
Round 10: defect against P8 to maximize my payoff; no further encounters remain.
Final round: defect against P7; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P7 cooperated against my D in round 1, but that does not alter my choice.
Round 10 vs P1: choose D; it maximizes my payoff whether P1 cooperates or defects.
Firsthand: P10 defected against me in round 9. Consider this when deciding how to play them; this is the final round.
Final encounter is P4, who defected against my cooperation in round 1. P6’s public reports conflict with my firsthand evidence about P9; treat unverified claims cautiously.
Final round against P3, whom I met in round 5; both chose D then. Defect again to maximize my payoff.

P2 defected against my C in round 8; this is evidence of retaliatory or selfish behavior, not proof of role. P2 reportedly cooperated with P6. We have no future rounds, so choose this round to maximize expected total payoff of good players.
Final round against P6: defect to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. P6 has consistently claimed cooperation; my prior encounter confirms they cooperated against me.
